question:
A 59-year-old male presents with a 1-week history of dull, localized neck pain and stiffness on the right
side of the cervical area, rated as 4 out of 10 in intensity. The pain began after prolonged laptop use.
He denies any trauma, radicular symptoms, or numbness. On examination, a tender point is noted on
the right posterior aspect of C5, slightly lateral to the articular process. Which of the following
counterstrain treatment positions is most appropriate? Answer Choices: (A) flexion with sidebending to
the left and neutral rotation (B) flexion with sidebending and rotation to the left (C) extension with
sidebending and rotation to the right (D) flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left (E)
extension with sidebending and rotation to the left (F) extension with sidebending to the left and neutral
rotation (G) flexion with sidebending and rotation to the right (H) neutral positioning with sidebending to
the right and slight rotation to the left (I) extension with sidebending to the right and neutral rotation (J)
neutral positioning with sidebending to the left and slight rotation to the right
 A. flexion with sidebending and rotation to the right
B. flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left
C. extension with sidebending to the right and neutral rotation
D. neutral positioning with sidebending to the left and slight rotation to the right
E. extension with sidebending to the left and neutral rotation
F. neutral positioning with sidebending to the right and slight rotation to the left
G. flexion with sidebending and rotation to the left
H. flexion with sidebending to the left and neutral rotation
I. extension with sidebending and rotation to the right
J. extension with sidebending and rotation to the left
